Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data scientist with experience developing predictive models, engineering features and building scheduled and batch-scoring workflows. Uses Python, SQL and GCP tools including BigQuery and Vertex AI Workbench. Seeking to grow into machine learning engineering and deepen production ML experience.

CORE SKILLS
Programming and analysis: Python, pandas, scikit-learn, SQL, R
Machine learning and statistics: LightGBM, XGBoost, SHAP, statsmodels, experimental design, Bayesian hierarchical models
Data and workflow tools: BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Looker, R Markdown
Engineering practices: pytest unit testing, Dockerfile authoring, Streamlit
Additional learning: PyTorch, torchvision

EXPERIENCE
Data Scientist | Thistlebox | 2022-Present
Work across experimentation, forecasting and churn modelling. In 2025, began writing pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage. Delivered internal training, “Stats for PMs,” three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | 2020-2022
Segmented customers and analysed tariffs using R and SQL. Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

SELECTED PROJECTS
Recipe Demand Forecasting | Thistlebox | 2022-2024
- Built weekly order forecasts six weeks ahead for each recipe and region using LightGBM with calendar, price and menu-position features.
- Ran forecasts as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook job, writing results to BigQuery for operations use in Looker.
- Improved WAPE from 23% to 14%; estimated food waste reduction was 9%.

Sequential A/B Testing Calculator | Thistlebox | 2023
- Built a Streamlit app for planning and analysing experiments with sequential boundaries, used by approximately 25 people in product and growth.
- Authored the app’s Dockerfile; the data platform team handled hosting and deployment on Cloud Run.

Churn Propensity and Retention Targeting | Thistlebox | 2024-2025
- Developed an XGBoost churn model scored weekly in BigQuery; retention offers were sent to top-decile customers.
- In a 10% holdout validation, churn was down 2.1 percentage points in the treated group.

Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small CNN in PyTorch on a public food images dataset, achieving approximately 80% accuracy as part of an online deep learning course.

EDUCATION
MSc in Statistics
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models
docs.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Machine Learning Engineer – Customer Support AI role at Quillstone Payments. I am a data scientist at Thistlebox, where I have developed forecasting and churn models and built tools for experimentation. I am interested in bringing that applied modelling experience to customer operations while growing further in production machine learning engineering.

My recent work includes a six-week recipe-demand forecasting workflow using LightGBM, scheduled through Vertex AI Workbench and writing results to BigQuery. It improved WAPE from 23% to 14%, with an estimated 9% reduction in food waste. I also developed a weekly-scored XGBoost churn model for retention targeting; in a 10% holdout validation, churn was down 2.1 percentage points in the treated group. These projects have given me practical experience with feature engineering, model evaluation and scheduled data workflows using Python and GCP tools.

I have also built a Streamlit app for sequential experiment planning and analysis, used by approximately 25 colleagues in product and growth. I wrote its Dockerfile, while the data platform team handled Cloud Run hosting and deployment. In 2025, I began adding pytest unit tests to forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage. I would be glad to bring this pragmatic, collaborative approach to Quillstone’s AI team as it works with product and engineering colleagues to help merchants and support agents.

Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my modelling and workflow experience could contribute to the team.

Kind regards,
Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
